title: Execution agrees with the transcript output
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$, and let $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ be an input pair. Running $p$ on $x$ and $y$ produces the same value as first executing $p$ on $(x,y)$ to obtain its syntactic transcript and then reading off the output value attached to the leaf of that transcript.
hypotheses_covered: p is a protocol over X, Y with output type α
an input pair (x, y) in X × Y
replaced:
For every protocol $p$ and input pair $xy$, running $p$ yields the same result as
reading the output from the computed transcript:
$p.\mathrm{run}(xy.1, xy.2) = \mathrm{Transcript.output}(p.\mathrm{transcript}(xy))$.
